title: Coefficient sections have no common zero
statement: For schemes X and S, an integer m ≥ 0 and any m+1 morphisms pr_i : X → P¹_S, let L be the ordered tensor product of pr_i^* O(1), and F_j its coefficient sections [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-sections]. At every point z of X, z belongs to the nonvanishing locus of some F_j [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], with 0 ≤ j ≤ m+1. No product universal property is required.

source.place: Proof, steps 2–3: coordinate pairs do not vanish, so the coefficient sections have no common zero (Stacks Tag 0A4F).

proof.text: Use the shared factorSection_eval lemma from SymmetricProductSectionsPermutation to evaluate each factor section as the adjunction-unit pullback of its homogeneous coordinate. The standard charts cover P¹, and each coordinate is nonvanishing on its chart. Nonvanishing survives tensor pullback, so at every point each coordinate pair contains a nonvanishing section.

At z let J be the factors whose second coordinate is not nonvanishing. For every i in J the first coordinate is nonvanishing; outside J the second is nonvanishing. The tensor-section locus formula shows the tensor term indexed by J is nonvanishing. Pullback and tensor products preserve invertibility.

For K distinct from J with the same cardinality, J is not contained in K. Choose i in J outside K. The tensor term indexed by K uses the vanishing second coordinate at i, so the tensor-section locus formula says that term has zero residue value. The residue-value criterion follows by identifying the residue tensor with the quotient of the stalk by its maximal ideal times the module.

Use the shared unitHomEquiv_sum_eval lemma from SymmetricProductSectionsPermutation: evaluation of unitHomEquiv on a sum of section morphisms is additive, as is evaluation in the residue fibre. Consequently the value of F_|J| is the value of the unique nonzero term J. Its residue value is nonzero, proving the claimed nonvanishing. The chosen cardinality is at most m+1, including J empty and J the full set.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetricProduct_sections_nonvanishing {S X : Scheme.{v}} (m : ℕ)
    (pr : Fin (m + 1) → (X ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{v} (Fin 2); S))) :
    ∀ z : X, ∃ j : ULift.{v} (Fin (m + 2)),
      z ∈ Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus (symmetricProductLineBundle pr)
        ((symmetricProductCoordinateSection pr j).val (Opposite.op ⊤))
